les: Galileo kyk self na die hemel

items.bewering: Galileo was 'n Italiaanse wiskundige en sterrekundige.
items.bron: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Galileo Galilei' (plato.stanford.edu/entries/galileo/): born in Pisa 1564, held the chairs of mathematics at Pisa and Padua, later 'Chief Mathematician and Philosopher' to the Grand Duke of Tuscany; his telescopic astronomy is described in the same entry.

items.bewering: Hy het later as Leonardo da Vinci gelewe, want hy is eers ná Leonardo se dood gebore.
items.bron: Leonardo died on 2 May 1519 at Clos Lucé, Amboise (Royal Collection Trust, rct.uk, 'Leonardo's death'; World History Encyclopedia). Galileo was born on 15 February 1564 (SEP). So 45 years after Leonardo's death; the order is right.

items.bewering: Hy het ook ná die seereise van Dias en Da Gama gelewe.
items.bron: Dias rounded the Cape in 1488; Da Gama sailed from Lisbon in July 1497 and reached Calicut in May 1498 (World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'; Museo Galileo, 'The circumnavigation of Africa'). Galileo was born in 1564 (SEP).

items.bewering: Sy werk staan aan die begin van wat ons vandag wetenskap noem.
items.bron: SEP, 'Galileo Galilei': since the 17th century many have seen him as the 'father' of modern science, and he is called 'the first real experimental scientist', though the entry treats that reputation with caution. The lesson's wording ('staan aan die begin van') is the softened form and does not say he founded science alone, so it holds.

items.bewering: In die Nederlande het iemand 'n nuwe kykglas gemaak wat ver dinge nader laat lyk.
items.bron: SEP: in July 1609 Galileo learned of 'a recent Dutch invention, the spyglass'. Dutch spectacle makers (Lippershey, Metius) applied for patents in 1608 (Museo Galileo, catalogue.museogalileo.it/indepth/Telescope.html). The lesson does not name an inventor, which avoids the disputed attribution.

items.bewering: Galileo het daarvan gehoor en sy eie teleskoop gebou. Hy het dit keer op keer verbeter en skerper gemaak.
items.bron: SEP: after hearing of the spyglass he built his own and produced 'a version capable of magnifying by twenty times'; he was 'remarkably careful to validate his instruments'. His first instruments magnified about 3x to 8x, later about 20x (Museo Galileo telescope entries).

items.bewering: Toe rig hy dit op die hemel.
items.bron: SEP and HPS Cambridge, 'Sidereus Nuncius: The Starry Messenger' (sites.hps.cam.ac.uk/starry/galsidnun.html): his telescopic observations of the Moon and Jupiter came in late 1609 and early 1610, after he had improved the instrument. The lesson does not say he was the first to point a telescope at the sky (Thomas Harriot drew the Moon through one a few months earlier), so the sentence is safe as written.

items.bewering: Hy het die teleskoop dus nie self uitgevind nie.
items.bron: SEP ('a recent Dutch invention, the spyglass'); Museo Galileo (Dutch patent applications 1608, before Galileo's first instrument in 1609).

items.bewering: Geleerdes van sy tyd het geglo die dinge in die hemel is glad en volmaak.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: HPS Cambridge, 'Sidereus Nuncius: The Starry Messenger': the Aristotelian world view held that everything above the Earth was perfect and incorruptible, and the Moon was taken to be smooth and perfectly spherical; Galileo's lunar observations were a blow to that view.

items.bewering: Deur sy teleskoop het Galileo berge en skaduwees op die maan gesien. Die maan is dus nie 'n gladde bal nie.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: SEP (the Moon's surface appeared mountainous); HPS Cambridge, 'The Starry Messenger' (the surface was not smooth and perfectly spherical but rough, with mountains; he worked out mountain heights from the shadows they cast).

items.bewering: By Jupiter het hy vier mane gesien wat om die planeet draai.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: SEP ('Jupiter has four moons'); HPS Cambridge, 'The Starry Messenger' (four satellites circling Jupiter, January 1610, named the Medicean stars). Jupiter has many more moons, but the lesson says how many he SAW, which is right.

items.bewering: Venus het ook fases net soos ons eie maan. Soms lyk Venus vol en rond en soms soos 'n dun stukkie lig.
items.blok: Wat hy in die hemel gesien het
items.bron: Oxford Museum of the History of Science, 'Galileo's most decisive telescopic observation: the phases of Venus, 1610-23' (cabinet.ox.ac.uk/node/6093): in 1610 Galileo saw Venus go through a full set of phases, from thin crescent to full disk and back, like the Moon. Mapping checked: the comparison carries the full cycle of shapes, which is the point. The one way Venus differs (it looks much larger as a crescent than when nearly full) is not something the comparison leads a learner to deny.

items.bewering: Byna almal in Galileo se tyd het geglo dat alles om die Aarde draai.
items.bron: SEP and HPS Cambridge, 'The Starry Messenger': the prevailing Aristotelian-Ptolemaic world view was geocentric. Note: by 1610 some astronomers held Tycho Brahe's system, in which the planets go round the Sun and the Sun goes round a still Earth, so 'alles' is slightly loose for that minority; 'byna almal' covers it and the sentence holds at this level.

items.bewering: Die vier mane wat hy by Jupiter gesien het, was van sy sterkste getuienis daarteen. Hier was dinge wat jy self kon sien draai om iets anders as die Aarde.
items.bron: HPS Cambridge, 'The Starry Messenger': the Jovian system was obviously not centred on the Earth, so Earth was not the only centre of motion; a Nature review (nature.com/articles/467398a) calls the Jovian moons the strongest argument yet against geocentrism. 'Van sy sterkste' (one of his strongest) is the safe form: historians often call the phases of Venus the more decisive observation (Oxford MHS), and the lesson does not say the moons were THE strongest.

items.bewering: Galileo het ook gesê dat die Aarde self om die Son beweeg.
items.bron: SEP: Galileo first openly backed Copernican heliocentrism in his 1613 Letters on Sunspots and became 'Copernicanism's best known advocate'.

items.bewering: Daardie idee was nie sy eie nie, want die geleerde Kopernikus het dit al voor hom voorgestel.
items.bron: SEP: the 'Copernican hypothesis'/'Copernican theory' Galileo defended; Copernicus's book (De revolutionibus, 1543) is the one suspended in 1616. Copernicus died in 1543, before Galileo was born.

items.bewering: Galileo se waarnemings deur die teleskoop het daardie ou idee ondersteun.
items.bron: SEP: the telescopic findings 'made a planetary earth more plausible, thereby supporting the Copernican hypothesis'. 'Ondersteun' (supported) is the right strength: the observations did not prove it, and also fitted Tycho's system (Oxford MHS; UNLV physics, 'Venus phases in Ptolemaic and Copernican systems').

items.bewering: Die kerkleiers van sy tyd het die idee verwerp, en party geleerdes ook.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: SEP: in 1616 Copernicus's book was suspended pending correction and Cardinal Bellarmine admonished Galileo not to teach or defend the Copernican theory; the same entry describes opposition from Aristotelian philosophers.

items.bewering: Hy is verhoor, en hy moes sê dat hy die idee terugtrek.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: SEP: in 1633 he was convicted of 'vehement suspicion of heresy' and made a formal abjuration.

items.bewering: Hy moes sy laaste jare in sy eie huis bly.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: SEP: the prison sentence was commuted to house arrest, served at his villa in Arcetri until his death in 1642; Museo Galileo (catalogue.museogalileo.it/indepth/VillaGioiello.html) and the University of Florence decree record (oajournals.fupress.net) date his move to the Villa Il Gioiello to December 1633. Note for the writer, not a fault: the villa was rented (lease of September 1631, Museo Galileo), so 'sy eie huis' holds in its ordinary sense of 'his own home', the point being the contrast with prison, but not in the sense of a house he owned. The first months of the house arrest were spent at the Villa Medici in Rome and the Archbishop of Siena's palace; 'laaste jare' still holds.

items.bewering: Hy is nie gemartel nie en ook nie in die tronk gesit nie.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: Maurice Finocchiaro, 'Prison and Torture as False but Well-Founded Myths' (UNLV Digital Scholarship, philosophy_fac_articles/118, 2021): Galileo was questioned under a verbal threat of torture but was not tortured; he was under house arrest during the 1633 trial and for the rest of his life and was never held in an actual prison, because the sentence of 'formal imprisonment' was never carried out. During the trial he was detained in rooms inside the Holy Office building, not a cell, which Finocchiaro counts as house arrest.

items.bewering: Galileo het verander hoe 'n mens weet of 'n antwoord reg is. 'n Antwoord moet klop met wat jy self kan sien en meet, selfs as almal iets anders glo.
items.blok: Die botsing en wat gebly het
items.bron: SEP: seen since the 17th century as a 'father' of modern science and an early experimental scientist who carefully validated his instruments and recorded measurements; historians credit him with quantitative experiment analysed mathematically. This is the standard interpretive view, simplified for Grade 6. SEP adds caution (he often used observation to test conclusions reached by reasoning), and he was not the only one changing method in his time; the lesson says he changed it, not that he did so alone, so it holds.

items.bewering: teleskoop: 'n Toestel om ver dinge mee te sien. Galileo s'n was 'n buis met lense wat ver dinge nader en groter laat lyk.
items.bron: Museo Galileo, catalogue entry 'Galileo's telescope' (catalogue.museogalileo.it/object/GalileosTelescope.html): a main tube with a biconvex objective lens and a plano-concave eyepiece, magnifying 14 times.

items.bewering: sterrekundige: Iemand wat die sterre en die planete bestudeer en meet.
items.bron: Standard meaning of 'astronomer'/'sterrekundige': one who studies the stars, planets and other heavenly bodies. The definition names only stars and planets, a simplification that leaves out the Moon and Sun but says nothing false. SEP's account of Galileo's measurements fits the 'meet' half.

items.bewering: fase: Die vorm waarin jy die maan of Venus op 'n sekere tyd sien.
items.bron: Oxford MHS, 'The phases of Venus, 1610-23': a phase is the lit shape of the Moon or Venus seen from Earth, from crescent to full. The definition gives the lesson's two examples and does not say only these two have phases (Mercury does too), so it holds when read alone.

items.bewering: verhoor: Die saak in 'n hof waar albei kante gehoor word.
items.bron: UFS/PanSALB legal term base (pokello.ufs.ac.za/s/PUO/item/30377): 'verhoor' = trial, 'a judicial examination of issues of fact or law for the purpose of determining the rights of the parties involved'. The definition is a fair general one. Galileo's court was the Inquisition, a church court, but the definition does not say what kind of court, and he was questioned and allowed to answer, so it does not mislead about his case.

opsomming: All 26 claims checked out, including every superlative and the Venus-Moon comparison, so nothing holds the lesson; the only thing worth a person's glance is that the house Galileo lived in under arrest was rented, so 'sy eie huis' is right as 'his own home' but not as a house he owned.
